# FDG8057

> DO implement `IEquatable<T>` any time you implement `IComparable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.6 IComparable&lt;T> and IEquatable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8057
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Type '{0}' implements IComparable<{1}> but not IEquatable<{1}>

FDG8057 reports a class or struct declared in source that implements IComparable<T> and does not implement IEquatable<T> for the same T. A type that inherits IComparable<T> from its base class is not reported, since the base class is. CA1036 is not mapped here: it asks for Equals and the operators, not for IEquatable<T> (FDG8058). Adding the interface adds to the public API without changing a signature; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Note that the reverse is not true, and not all types can support ordering.

```csharp
public struct Decimal : IComparable<Decimal>, IEquatable<Decimal> {
   ...
}
```
